subject: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume + peak TPS
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Devon Park <devon@finpay.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena@finpay.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume + peak TPS

Hi Devon / Lena,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can put together a tailored hosted-API cost estimate:

- Recap: FinPay is evaluating Redwood Hosted API to power contextual finance assistant (document parsing + chat + short generative responses).
- To size pricing accurately we need:
  1) Expected monthly token volume (input + output) , if you have a range that's fine (e.g., 50M-150M).
  2) Peak TPS (approx requests/sec at peak) and any strict latency SLOs.
  3) Target unit economics / budget (e.g., target $/1M tokens or monthly budget range).
  4) Timeline to production and any compliance/SLA requirements.

I attached a small template you can drop numbers into (FinPay_token_estimates.xlsx) , if you prefer, a quick reply with ballparks is totally fine.

From experience, at ~100M tokens/month we often discuss committed pricing or small volume discounts; for hosted API we can also offer a short intro credit if you want to validate before committing.

Proposed next step: if you can share ballpark numbers by EOD Thursday (Jun 4) I'll run a cost model and follow up with a recommended plan + price points. If it helps we can also do a 20-minute call to review.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: FinPay_token_estimates.xlsx (xlsx, 24KB)]

From: Devon Park <devon@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena@finpay.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume + peak TPS

Hi Marissa,

Great recap, appreciate the template. Sharing our early estimates below and attaching the filled sheet. These are ballpark and likely to evolve as we finalize our usage patterns:

- Expected monthly tokens (input+output): 80M-150M tokens/month (first 90 days we expect closer to 80-100M, steady state 120-150M).
- Peak TPS: ~6-10 requests/sec during business hours (rough average peak ~8 TPS).
- Typical request size: ~600 tokens (avg) input, ~120 tokens output (so tokens per request ~720).
- Target unit economics: ideally $10-$20 per 1M tokens; budget range $3k-$5k/month initially.
- Timeline: pilot in July, production by Sep if things look good.

Attached: FinPay_token_estimates.xlsx (filled). Can you run the model on the higher end (150M) and share cost at tiered volumes? Also curious what discounts or committed rates you offer for hosted API versus Dedicated.

Thanks,
Devon
Head of Product, FinPay
[Attachment: FinPay_token_estimates.xlsx (xlsx, 28KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Devon Park <devon@finpay.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena@finpay.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 11:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume + peak TPS

Thanks Devon, this is super helpful. I ran a quick pass with our pricing models and attached a concise pricing sheet (Redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf). High-level notes:

- At 80-100M tokens/month (hosted, on-demand): estimated list cost is around $X per 1M tokens (I put ballpark ranges on the sheet).
- At 120-150M tokens/month we can discuss graduated discounts and an intro committed rate that moves toward your $10-$20/1M target; committed 3-6 month volume credits can materially reduce unit price.
- Peak TPS ~8 is well within hosted capacity; if you need strict p50/p95 latency SLOs or higher guaranteed concurrency we may recommend Dedicated or a Reserved SLA add-on.

Questions / next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether the 6-10 TPS peak is sustained or short bursts? If sustained we should model concurrency differently.
2) Please confirm your target $/1M tokens to the single number you care about so I can create 2-3 proposal options (on-demand hosted, 3-month commit, 6-month commit).
3) If you can share a 90-day volume forecast (day-by-day or weekly bins) that will let us present more accurate burst/peak pricing.

I've CC'd Alex for pricing approval and Sean for SRE/latency guidance. If you'd like, I can schedule a 30-min follow-up on Mon Jun 8 to walk through the proposals.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume + peak TPS, FinPay (FP-2026-43)

Internal, quick summary and ask: please review and advise on pricing flexibility for FinPay (deal FP-2026-43). Key numbers from the customer:

- Monthly tokens: 80M-150M (90-day ramp: ~80-100M, steady state ~120-150M)
- Peak TPS: ~6-10 (avg peak ~8 TPS), typical request ~720 tokens/request
- Target unit economics: customer ideally wants $10-$20 per 1M tokens; current stated budget $3k-$5k/month at pilot stage
- Timeline: pilot July, production Sep

Ask: can Alex/Ben run committed vs on-demand pricing scenarios (3-month and 6-month commits) that hit ~ $10-$15 / 1M if possible while preserving margin? Sean, any concerns on our hosted capacity given peak TPS and expected token/request size?

I plan to propose 3 options to the customer next week:
- On-demand hosted (no commit) - standard list pricing
- 3-month commit - moderate discount, introductory credit for pilot
- 6-month commit - steeper discount, priority routing + higher concurrency guardrails

Thanks, Marissa
